recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed unless a future work-group decision changes the modern BackboneType abstraction itself.
issue_request: FHIR-17404 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-I STU3 clarification request asking whether ElementDefinition should be treated as a BackboneElement/modifier-extension-capable type because the ElementDefinition page and Datatypes page appeared inconsistent. The approved resolution was to make it consistently clear that it is a backbone element.
initial_application: The issue was applied in svn revision 14035, represented by git commit cd611f6d04dcd2087501f6c40ddaf5762076a31b, which changed the ElementDefinition spreadsheet root type from Structure to BackboneElement.
additional_context: The current build split the old BackboneElement-based datatype treatment into BackboneType. source/fhir.ini actively includes ElementDefinition as a datatype and BackboneType as normative infrastructure; source/datatypes/elementdefinition.xml derives ElementDefinition from BackboneType; source/datatypes/backbonetype.xml defines BackboneType.modifierExtension; and source/types.html plus source/datatypes.html list ElementDefinition among datatypes that may carry modifier extensions. The 2019 abstract type-framework refactor changed the literal base from BackboneElement to BackboneType without losing modifierExtension semantics.
reconciliation: No source change was made because the current source is already internally consistent and preserves the FHIR-17404 decision. Adding redundant prose to elementdefinition.html would duplicate generated/inherited type information and risk drift.

related_jiras.note: Earlier datatype/modifier-extension work explains the family of modifier-extension-capable datatypes that FHIR-17404 clarified.
Search surfaced this later modifierExtension summary issue, but it concerns DomainResource/BackboneElement summary flags rather than ElementDefinition specialization.
